body:
I think the description is a bit lengthy and verbose. I attempted to simplify it:

```suggestion
			[b]VRAM Compressed:[/b] Reduced quality, low memory usage, low size on disk, slow import. This mode should be used for high-resolution textures in 3D to reduce VRAM usage, but should be avoided for textures in 2D and low-resolution textures due to compression artifacts being more visible. This mode compresses to a platform-specific format, which may look slightly different across platforms, and may require exports targeting multiple platforms (like web) to ship multiple formats, increasing the size on disk.
```

 			[b]VRAM Uncompressed:[/b] Original quality, high memory usage, highest size on disk, fastest import.
-			[b]Basis Universal:[/b] Reduced quality, low memory usage, lowest size on disk, slow import. Only use for textures in 3D scenes, not for 2D elements.
+			[b]Basis Universal:[/b] Reduced quality, low memory usage, lowest size on disk, slowest import. Similar use cases as VRAM Compressed, but performs runtime transcoding from a single format to a native VRAM-compressed format supported by the device the project is running on. This avoids the potential need to include multiple VRAM-compressed formats in the PCK file for multi-platform support. The downside is that the transcoding process slows down texture loading times.
body:
I think this description is a bit lengthy. I attempted to simplify it:

```suggestion
			[b]Basis Universal:[/b] Reduced quality, low memory usage, lowest size on disk, slowest import. Similar to VRAM Compressed, but compresses to a universal format and transcodes it to a platform-specific format at runtime. This makes textures slower to load, but avoids the need to ship multiple platform-specific formats in some exports (like web).
```

body:
It's not about texture resolution, but whether the texture is meant to be pixel art (precise color palette).

Sometimes, you want to use VRAM compression on small textures because you have a lot of them, or because they cover a tiny surface in 3D space. This is why https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/62023 was reverted, as it affected *all* low-resolution textures used in 3D, not just those with a pixel art style.

I've incorporated the latter part of the suggestion still.
